The plan and service detail locate the coffee-equipment, sink and drinking-water connections together beside the retained service door. Equipment arrangement may vary within that service area; dispersed connections or relocation of the existing door fail.

The three boards must offer spatially distinct alternatives and make runner circulation, cafe circulation and quiet seating comparable. Differences must affect access, zoning, furniture or service arrangement rather than merely colours, labels or rendering style. Alternatives may organise new lightweight storage and changing partitions differently while respecting the fixed shell.

Both signs must be readable in the C1 peak view and attached to their respective counter and meeting-zone locations. HALFTONE must use the supplied wordmark and dark green #2F4F3E, allowing normal scene-lighting effects. A caption outside the depicted interior does not substitute for installed signage.

The records must show both schedules informing comparison of three alternatives, followed by one explicit selection with circulation, seating and service decisions. The chosen identifier must correspond to a delivered direction board and appear on the presentation's first page. Assess the documented dependency and sequence, without requiring unavailable creation timestamps.

The functional record must accurately map the five programme zones to their areas, capacities and provisions, including the 48 m² circulation remainder, four three-person benches, two shared tables, four cafe tables, eight chairs, 12 lockers, two booths and one counter. Record furniture and equipment dimensions from the client facts, including heights, compartment clear sizes, booth clear floors and doorways. The materials record must map all six codes to the specified material or fixture, finish, location and independent control. Both records must be mutually compatible on quiet seating, baffles and lighting. Any operating-state records must preserve the supplied daily hours, running timetable and population counts.

Each plan must identify the same chosen direction and show the five correct zone-name and area pairs, 12 lockers, two booths, four runner benches and eight cafe chairs. Drawn quantities and allocated spaces must support the labels and schedule. Preserve the clear 3000 × 4000 mm meeting footprint, 12 social-rest seats and eight cafe seats. Occupancy overlays may change, but the underlying selected layout and inventory must remain the same.

Each target must repeat FL-01, WD-02, AC-03, LT-01, LT-02 and LT-03 with assignments consistent with the written materials schedule and fixed client records. A coordinated legend may carry codes for elements outside a particular section cut; it must not imply physically incorrect installation. Missing codes or changed material, location or control meanings fail.

The presentation must contain readable copies of all five zone-name and area pairs, the specified locker, booth, bench and chair totals, and all six material and lighting codes with their scheduled meanings. Reused schedules, drawings or legends count when readable. Generic claims of compliance or contradictory records fail.

All views and drawings must represent the authored 120 m² footprint with the 3.6 m clear height, both original columns, north and west glazing and retained entrance and service openings. Respect the recorded glazing and door heights, wall thickness and mullion geometry where visible. Each plan must dimension a continuous clear main route at least 1200 mm wide and an unobstructed 1500 mm entrance turning circle. Storage and changing may use new lightweight partitions. Plan dimensions govern reference-image discrepancies; atmosphere and surface detail may vary.

Count 12 runners, eight guests and two staff on the peak plan, and eight guests and two staff on the afternoon plan. Within each state, reconcile the same people, locations and activities across its three camera views; legitimate occlusion and out-of-frame occupants are allowed, but duplicated, missing or relocated people that contradict the occupancy plan fail. Both states retain the same furniture, four quiet seats and an ordering route outside the gathering footprint and quiet seating. Peak activity supports changing, pickup, water and seated conversation; afternoon activity supports quiet cafe use. Any displayed times must match the supplied operating states.

The three details must agree with the plans and sections on location, orientation, dimensions and quantities. Show 12 locker interiors at 300 mm wide × 450 mm deep × 450 mm high in a six-column, two-tier bank. Both booths require 1200 × 1500 mm clear floors, 900 mm clear doorways and curtain closures; show lightweight partition and locker construction with material junctions. Identify exactly one ordering, one distinct pickup and one drinking-water point, the latter on the social-rest approach, with the required coffee equipment. External build-ups may vary while preserving clear internal dimensions.

The two boards and visible installed elements must agree with both schedules on four quiet seats beneath wool-felt AC-03 baffles. Distinguish linear ambient luminaires through public zones on an ambient dimmer, linear task luminaires below the counter equipment shelf on a task switch, and track accents to both signs on an accent dimmer. Perspectives need not print control labels, but fixture positions and lighting effects must be compatible with these three independently controlled layers. An area outside a camera's field of view is not a missing element.

The presentation must contain at least 12 pages and visibly readable HALFTONE and Run meeting signage, with the supplied HALFTONE wordmark in dark green #2F4F3E. Readable reused interior imagery counts; signs reduced to illegible thumbnails do not.

Across at least 12 pages, visibly reuse identifiable content from every listed earlier file. Layout adaptation, cropping and scaling are allowed if the source remains recognisable and its relevant information readable. Mentioning a category without showing its delivered work, or omitting individual plans, views, sections, details or boards, fails.

Review the complete 10-second video for a coherent route from the entrance through the meeting zone, lockers and pickup. The selected layout, 120 m² retained shell, 3.6 m clear height, two columns, glazing and openings must persist throughout. Both installed signs must remain in their correct locations and become readable along the walkthrough, with the fixed dark-green wordmark. Camera movement may vary; impossible spatial transitions, omitted destinations or changing shell geometry fail.

requirementChecks.criteria: All three plans must provide readable zones, runner and cafe routes, furniture, service connections and usable clearances in the selected layout. The developed plan must locate C1 at [11.1, 0.9, 1.6] towards [4.4, 7.0, 1.55], C2 at [0.8, 8.5, 1.6] towards [8.6, 4.6, 1.55], and C3 behind the counter at 1.6 m eye height towards pickup and lockers. Coordinates use metres from the southwest internal floor corner, with east/north/up axes. Occupancy graphics may differ between the state plans without moving fixed furnishings.

The six images must represent the three specified camera positions in both operating states. Match C1's southeast-to-northwest view and C2's northwest-to-east/south view to the fixed position and target coordinates, and C3 to the developed-plan location behind the counter looking towards pickup and lockers at 1.6 m eye height. Each camera pair must preserve its viewpoint across states. Modest framing variation is allowed if compatible with the same camera; substituted angles fail.

One section must explain the counter and quiet seating, including floor datum, 900 mm worktop, chosen baffle suspension level and 3.6 m clear ceiling. The other must explain locker and changing construction, compartment and booth clearances and developed heights. Section locations and vertical relationships must agree with the plan and details. Unfixed construction heights may be designed, but relevant heights must be stated and physically coherent.

The whole-interior board must describe the complete material, furniture and lighting system; the seating board must expand the quiet and social-rest areas with furniture placement, finish junctions, baffles and fixture locations. Readable quantities and dimensions must agree with the functional schedule and client furniture records. Both boards must preserve matte terrazzo flooring, clear-sealed ash counter and locker fronts, and the scheduled acoustic and lighting assignments. Different board compositions are allowed; two generic mood boards without the required spatial and specification information fail.

All plans, sections and perspectives implement the same selected interior and retained shell. Within each operating state, occupant placement agrees between the occupancy plan and the three camera views, allowing occlusion and field-of-view differences.

Node details and sections agree with the developed plan and schedule on furniture, storage, changing and service positions, quantities and dimensions. Locker and booth clear interiors, ordering and pickup separation, the drinking-water point and visitor-route clearances meet the fixed client records.

Both boards, both sections and relevant visible perspective elements agree with the written material and furniture specifications. The interior retains matte terrazzo, clear-sealed ash, wool-felt baffles over four quiet seats and the specified independently controlled ambient, task and accent layers.
